A copper alloy Roman Aucissa brooch dating from AD 43 - 75. The strip brooch has a head formed by rolling the strip forwards to form a tube for the axis bar. Iron corrosion obscures most of the area (presumably from the axis bar) but the head does not appear to be inscribed "Aucissa" as on the brooches which gave this class their name. Only the head of the hinged copper alloy pin survives. A transverse band of ropework decorates the head, and then the strongly arched bow is fluted. A central ridge decorated with ropework is flanked by a channel on each side, and beyond them is another band of ropework along both edges of the bow.
